CITY OF AVALON PLANNING COMMISSION AGENDA
  City Hall Council Chambers ∙ 410 Avalon Canyon Road, Avalon, CA
  Regular Meeting – February 19, 2024 at 5:00 p.m.

  This meeting is viewable in person at the Council Chambers or via livestream:

  Facebook: (http://www.facebook.com/CityOfAvalonOfficial)
  YouTube (http://www.youtube.com/cityofavalonca)
  Website (http://www.cityofavalon.com/meetings)
  Cable (Catalina Broadband Solutions Channel 3)

  The Council Chambers can accommodate a maximum of 30 participants, at which point
  the general public may address the Planning Commission on an agenda item by waiting
  in the City Hall Court Yard and entering the Chambers one at a time. No one will be
  admitted into the Council Chambers who is ill or exhibiting symptoms of COVID-19. The
  Planning Commission is not accepting live comments electronically at this time.

  The public can submit written comments prior to 12:00 p.m. 3 days prior to the meeting
  in person to the Planning Department at City Hall or via email to
  dromo@cityofavalon.com.

  Staff reports for each agenda item are posted a minimum of 72 hours prior to the
  meeting and are available for review in person or on the City website at
  http://www.cityofavalon.com.

  In compliance with the Americans with Disability Act, if you need special assistance to participate
  in this meeting, please contact Gabrielle Morones, City Clerk’s office (310) 510-0220 ext. 119.
  Notification 48 hours prior to the meeting will enable the City to make reasonable arrangements
  to ensure accessibility to this meeting. (28 CFR 35. 102-35.104 ADA Title II). All public records
  relating to an agenda item on this agenda are available for the public inspection at the time the
  records are distributed to all, or a majority of all, members of the Planning Commission. Such
  records shall be available at City Hall located at 410 Avalon Canyon Road.

  CALL TO ORDER

  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE/ROLL CALL

  ORAL COMMUNICATION: This is the time for any member of the public to address the
  Planning Commission on any matter not on the agenda that is within the subject matter
  jurisdiction of the City. The Brown Act, with limited exceptions, does not allow the
  Commission or staff to discuss or take action on issues brought forth under Public
  Comment. Concerns may be referred to staff or placed on the next available agenda.
  Please note that comments from the public will also be taken on each agenda item.
  Comments shall be limited to three minutes per person.

   AVALON PLANNING COMMISSION
  STAFF REPORT – PC# 2846
  Wednesday, February 19, 2025

  Application File: CUP, VAR, SPR, CDP
Item No.  – Public Hearing  Submitted by: Kelly Ribuffo, Contract Planner

A Public Hearing considering a Conditional Use Permit, Variance, Site Plan, and Coastal
Development Permit to allow interior and exterior remodeling of an existing restaurant building,
including installation of an elevator and construction of a roof deck, in the Commercial (C) zone.
The Proposed Project is categorically exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act
(CEQA) per State CEQA Guidelines 15301 (Class 1 - Existing Facilities). The proposed project is
located within the appealable area of the Coastal Zone.

  Applicant:  Ralph Gentile Architects
  Owner:  Island Food & Stuff LLC
  Files:  CUP, VAR, SPR, CDP
  Location of Project: 111 Clarissa Avenue
  APN:  7480-015-017
  PC #:  2846
  File Date:  5/19/2023
  General Plan:  Commercial (C)
  Zone:  Commercial (C)

  BACKGROUND

  1
   Project Vicinity
  General Plan  Zoning  Current Use
 On-Site  Commercial (C)  Commercial (C)  Restaurant (Mi Casita)
 North  Commercial (C)  Commercial (C)  Restaurant (NDMK Fish
  House)

  Residential (including Catalina
  Yamaha and Catalina Sea Spa)

Existing Site:

The project site is located on a regularly shaped parcel addressed 111 Clarissa Avenue. The parcel
is situated south of Crescent Avenue and north of Third Street. The lot is relatively flat, with a
gentle slope from west to east.

The project site is currently developed with a two-story restaurant building constructed in 1974 in
a Spanish/Mexican Colonial inspired style. Characteristic design features include clay tile roofing,

  2
 arched window openings, and decorative glazed tile on the first floor. The footprint of the building
covers the entire lot, with no planters or vegetation present on the property.

Existing Area Context:

All abutting properties are in the Commercial zone and represent a mix of commercial buildings
and mixed use buildings with residential uses on upper floors. Surrounding uses include the
Pavilion Hotel (513 Crescent Avenue) to the west, mixed use commercial with residential (112,
114, and 117 Clarissa Avenue) to the south and east, and NDMK Fish House (109 Clarissa
Avenue) to the north.

Entitlement and Permit History:

The following entitlements have been granted for the project site:

  •  PC# 1205 – Approval of a 1-foot encroachment permit into the public right-of-way for the
  roof overhang along Clarissa Avenue (December 1985).
  •  PC# 1269 – Conditional Use Permit for conversion of 230 square foot employee housing
  area to a bar for an existing restaurant (January 1987).
  •  PC# 1311 – Conditional Use Permit, Site Plan, and Variance to remove employee housing,
  replace with a patio, and construction a new 2-bedroom unit on a new second floor
  (December 1987).
  •  PC# 1577 – Variance for gross lot coverage not to exceed 99% and allow a 0-foot rear
  setback (October 1994).
  •  PC# 1625 – Variance for off-street parking spaces, exceed maximum allowable lot
  coverage, and maximum floor area to add second story with open deck (December 1995).
  •  PC# 2056 – Variance to legalize a 70 square foot roof addition for storage as an existing
  nonconforming condition (July 2003).

A demolition permit (Permit# 25026) for interior demolition was granted on February 6, 2025 and
is currently in progress.

  PROJECT DESCRIPTION

The applicant, Ralph Gentile Architects, on behalf of Island Food & Stuff LLC, proposes to
remodel the exterior façade and interior of the existing 4,498 square foot Mi Casita Restaurant and
construct a new 1,157 square foot roof deck addition. Key exterior upgrades will focus on refreshed
finishes, updated lighting, and improved pedestrian appeal and accessibility. Interior
improvements will include remodeled dining areas, restrooms, and kitchen facilities. The addition
of the third-floor rooftop dining deck will provide patrons with a new outdoor dining option and
views of Avalon Bay.

Hours of operation for restaurant and interior bar are 7:00 AM to 11:00 PM Sunday through
Thursday and 7:00 AM to 12:00 AM Friday and Saturday. Hours of operation for the roof deck and
rooftop food service operations are proposed to be 9:00AM to 9:00PM Sunday through Thursday
and 9:00 AM to 10:00 PM Friday and Saturday.

  3
 The restaurant currently operates with a California Alcoholic Beverage Control (ABC) Type 47
(On-Sale General Eating Place) license which allows the sale of beer, wine, and liquor. The
applicant proposes no changes to their ABC license except the ability to extend service to the roof
deck once constructed.

Additional information regarding the operation of the proposed business and architectural plans
are included in Attachments 2 and 3 of this report.

Seating Phasing:

Per adopted tariffs with the California Public Utilities Commission, Southern California Edison
(SCE) calculated water allocations for restaurant uses based on total seating count.

Remodeling of the building and construction of the roof deck is proposed to take place in one
phase. In order to operate within the existing water allocation for the business, the applicant
proposed to limit seating within the restaurant at or below the existing seating count until SCE
grants an additional water allocation to the restaurant. The schedule for SCE to release the
additional water allocation is unknown at this time.

Currently, the restaurant has 182 seats distributed over two floors. Phase 1 of the seating plan
proposes 172 seats distributed over two floors and the roof deck, below the existing seating count.
Phase 2 of the seating plan proposes 190 total seats over two floors and the roof deck once
additional water is allocated by SCE. A detailed seating diagrams and a summary table are
provided on Sheet A1.00.02 of Attachment 3.

Development Standards:

The proposed project must comply with development standards set forth in Avalon Municipal
Code (AMC) Section 9-6.204 for the C zoning district as follows:

* Existing developments are presumed to be legally nonconforming for the purpose of this analysis.
** Per AMC Sec. 9-3.606, the area of uncovered roof deck does not count towards calculation of floor area.

  AUTHORIZING GUIDELINES

Avalon Municipal Code (AMC) Sections 9-8.401, 9-8.203.a and 9-8.103.a authorize the Planning
Commission to review and take action on the subject applications for a Conditional Use Permit,
Variance, Site Plan, and Coastal Development Permit.

  DISCUSSION AND ANALYSIS

Issue 1: Variances for Height

Per AMC Chapter 9-8.405, variances from development standards may be permitted by the
Planning Commission where the special circumstances may deprive a property of privileges
enjoyed by other property in the vicinity and under identical zoning classification, the property is
not granted special privileges beyond those available to similar properties, does not permit a use
that is otherwise not allowed, and complies with the Avalon Local Coastal Program.

In the Commercial zone, the maximum allowable building height within 350 feet of the mean high
tide line is 28 feet. The applicant is requesting a variance to allow up to 32 feet in height to
accommodate the enclosure for the staircase enclosures and Limited Use Limited Access (LULA)
elevator shaft. The stairs and elevators will facilitate access to the roof deck and rooftop
mechanical area. Both staircases and the elevator are required by the California Building Code for
accessibility compliance. The roof deck improvements otherwise have a maximum height of 22
feet 10 inches to the top of the parapet wall, well under the required height.

It is the opinion of staff that the request meets the findings for granting of a variance. The variance
request is limited in scope and will allow the operator to bring access to the rooftop in compliance
with code mandated accessibility requirements. This is a regulatory constraint that is applicable to
all properties within the Commercial zone, and to all properties generally throughout the city, and
that in this instance limit properties for developing to the full extent permitted in the municipal
code. The height required to accommodate the staircase enclosure and LULA elevator is within
the average height required for such installations. Purchase of specialized equipment could

  5
 potentially reduce the height of the elevator tower, but a height variance would still be required
for both the elevator tower and staircase enclosure due to construction limitations.

Therefore, the proposed variances may be granted in conformance with the findings of the
municipal code, as the strict application of the Zoning Ordinance would deprive the subject
property of privileges enjoyed by other property in the vicinity and under identical zoning
classification.

Issue 2: Rooftop Deck Operations

According to the applicant, the rooftop deck will provide an expanded dining area for customers
with views of Avalon Bay. Full food and drink service will be provided, consistent with the rest
of the restaurant. The rooftop deck will be open from 9:00 AM until 9:00 PM Sunday through
Thursday and 9:00 AM to 10:00 PM on Friday and Saturday. The roof deck may be reserved for
private events during the same operating hours. Events will be required to apply for a Special
Event Permit (AMC Chapter 4-6) and demonstrate compliance with all city code requirements.

Use of the rooftop deck has the potential to create noise nuisance for surrounding properties.
Operations must be consistent with Avalon Municipal Code Section 5-13.08 for a building within
Noise District 2, which states that it is “unlawful to use or operate or cause to be used or operated
outdoors any radio receiving set, sound amplifying equipment, television set, or other machine or
device which produces or reproduces sound in such a manner as to be plainly audible from the real
property line on which the sound amplifying equipment is located unless permitted by Special Use
Permit.” The applicant is not requesting approval of a Special Use Permit at this time.

It is the opinion of staff that with limited hours of operation and the requirement for a Special
Event Permit for events, the proposed roof deck is compatible with the intent of the C zone and
should not cause undue noise nuisance to surrounding properties. The roof deck is surrounded by
a glass windscreen along the parapet wall, and the rooftop kitchen and mechanical equipment
building is placed to provide additional separation between the deck and adjacent residential uses
to the south.

Furthermore, prior to issuance of a building permit, the applicant shall prepare a lighting plan that
includes the location, type, and illumination level of all proposed exterior light fixtures for staff
review to address potential light nuisances before exterior remodeling begins on the property.

  GENERAL PLAN, LAND USE, AND ZONING COMPLIANCE

Annual Growth Policy:

The growth policy provides that new commercial development would only be permitted with
confirmation from Southern California Edison Company (“SCE”) that adequate fresh water is
available. The project involves permitting of modifications to a commercial business which
requires an allocation for water service. On February 12, 2025, SCE confirmed that no additional
water allocation is required to complete Phase 1 of the project seating plan (up to 182 seats). The
applicant has been placed on the waitlist for Phase 2 of the seating plan (up to 190 seats). Staff has

  6
 conditioned the project in Condition No. 14 to require confirmation of a water allocation for Phase
2 of the project seating plan prior to expansion of seating capacity of the restaurant. Staff
recommends that, with this Condition No. 14, the Planning Commission make the finding that the
proposed project is in compliance with the 2025 Annual Growth Policy.

Conditional Use Permit:

The proposed project must be granted a Conditional Use Permit per AMC Section 9-6.203.a.1.
AMC Section 9-8.404 sets forth the required findings for approval of a Conditional Use Permit as
follows:

  1. The proposed conditional use shall conform with and carry out the certified Land Use
  Plan for the area. (AMC Section 9-8.404.a.1)

  The proposed project implements the following General Plan Policies:

  Policy II-9 of the Land Use Element:

  “Encourage infill of the City Center area and where appropriate, increase the intensity of
  development on vacant and underutilized properties, in lieu of expanded development
  outward into Avalon’s hillsides, natural areas and open space.”

  The project proposed to remodel an existing restaurant building and add a new accessible
  roof deck. The existing building has operated as a restaurant for over 50 years and has been
  added onto as the business has grown over time. The project is designed to maximize the
  density of development on the property in the urbanized center of Avalon. Remodeling and
  expansion of the existing restaurant within the footprint of the existing lot does not
  contribute to outward expansion into the surrounding natural areas or open spaces at the
  perimeter of the city.

  2. The nature, condition, and development of adjacent uses, buildings and structures
  shall be considered and no proposed conditional use shall be permitted where such
  use will adversely affect or be materially detrimental to said adjacent uses, buildings
  and structures. (AMC Section 9-8.404.a.2)

  The proposed project is consistent with adjacent land uses and building types. The project
  site located in a commercial dense area of the flats, developed with two and three-story
  commercial and mixed use building. With the addition of the roof deck, the building will
  still fit within the overall massing and scale of surrounding development.

  Operations of the restaurant, including roof deck, must comply with Avalon Municipal
  Code Section 5-13.08 for a building within Noise District 2. Sound must be contained to
  the boundaries of the property and no events will be permitted without the granting of a
  Special Event Permit by the City Manager. Furthermore, the accessory staircase enclosure
  and mechanical equipment on the rooftop of the building is intentionally placed to
  minimize potential noise impacts to the residential units directly adjacent to the south.
  Condition No. 7 limits hours of operation of the roof deck for the roof deck and rooftop
  7
   food service operations shall be 9:00AM to 9:00PM Sunday through Thursday and 9:00
  AM to 10:00 PM Friday and Saturday, which further limits the potential for noise nuisance
  to adjacent properties.

  Furthermore, prior to issuance of a building permit, the applicant shall prepare a lighting
  plan that includes the location, type, and illumination level of all proposed exterior light
  fixtures for staff review to address potential light nuisances before exterior remodeling
  begins on the property.

  Therefore, the proposed project will not adversely affect or be materially detrimental to
  said adjacent uses, buildings and structures.

3. The site for a proposed conditional use shall be adequate in size and shape to
  accommodate the yards, walls, fences, parking and loading facilities, landscaping and
  other development features prescribed in this chapter or as required as a condition
  in order to integrate said use with the uses in the neighborhood. (AMC Section 9-
  8.404.a.3)

  With the requested variance for building height, the proposed project complies with all
  development standards as set forth in AMC for development on the project site in the
  Commercial (C) zone. The property was previously granted a variance from on-site parking
  requirements (PC# 1635, December 1995). Due to its proximity to Crescent Avenue and
  the Cabrilla Mole, this area of “the flats” receives high volumes of pedestrian traffic, with
  some pick up and drop off vehicle traffic. There have been no reported traffic issues
  associated with the restaurant, and seating capacity of the restaurant will not substantially
  increase beyond existing levels. It is anticipated that existing sidewalks, combined with the
  adjacent loading and drop-off zones, will ensure that traffic associated with operation of
  the business will not interfere with circulation along Clarissa Avenue.

  The project site is located in an area with access to all necessary utilities and services to
  support the proposed use, including electric, water, gas, sewer, saltwater, and internet.

4. The site for a proposed conditional use shall be served by highways and streets
  adequate in width and improved as necessary to carry the kind and quantity of traffic
  such use would generate. (AMC Section 9-8.404.a.4)

  The project site is located on the west side of Clarissa Avenue between Crescent Avenue
  and Third Street. This is a heavily traveled area, and all three streets are identified as Major
  Circulation Facility in the General Plan Circulation Element. There have been no reported
  traffic issues associated with the restaurant, and seating capacity of the restaurant will not
  substantially increase beyond existing levels. It is anticipated that existing sidewalks,
  combined with the adjacent loading and drop-off zones, will ensure that traffic associated
  with operation of the business will not interfere with circulation along Clarissa Avenue.

5. The proposed conditional use shall be consistent with and carry out the purpose and
  intent of the underlying zone. (AMC Section 9-8.404.a.5)

  8
   Per AMC Section 9-6.201, the C zoning district is established to provide areas for the
  development of business and professional offices, services and related uses to conveniently
  serve the public. Restaurants, bars and cafes are permitted with approval of a Conditional
  Use Permit.

  The project site has operated as a restaurant for over 50 years, with entitlements granted as
  the building and business has grown over time. The project proposes to remodel the interior
  and exterior of the building, including the addition of a roof deck with food and drink
  service. This will provide a new dining option for residents and visitors to the city.

  Alcoholic beverage sales are customary with food service in the heart of the downtown
  commercial zone. The restaurant currently operates with a California Alcoholic Beverage
  Control (ABC) Type 47 (On-Sale General Eating Place) license which allows the sale of
  beer, wine, and liquor. The applicant proposes no changes to their ABC license except the
  ability to extend service to the new roof deck.

  Therefore, the proposed project is consistent with the underlying intent of the zone and
  compatible with surrounding development in the vicinity of the project site.

Variance:

The proposed project must be granted a Variance for height per AMC Section 9-6.204.d.1. AMC
Section 9-8.405 sets forth the required findings for approval of a Variance as follows:

  1. Variances from the terms of the Zoning Ordinance shall be granted only when,
  because of special circumstances applicable to the property including size, shape,
  topography, location or surroundings, the strict application of the Zoning Ordinance
  deprives such property of privileges enjoyed by other property in the vicinity and
  under identical zoning classification.

  The urban fabric of Avalon is relatively compact, with approximately 80-90 acres of
  existing development already located within the valley floor and the immediately
  surrounding hillsides. Individually owned lots in Avalon comprise less than 1% of the total
  city acreage. Therefore, it is important to maximize the use of land within the city within
  the development parameters of each zoning district, so long as it is consistent with overall
  community character.

  In the Commercial zone, the maximum allowable building height within 350 feet of the
  mean high tide line is 28 feet. The applicant is requesting a variance to allow up to 32 feet
  in height to accommodate the enclosure for the staircase enclosures and Limited Use
  Limited Access (LULA) elevator shaft. The stairs and elevators will facilitate access to the
  roof deck and rooftop mechanical area. Both staircases and the elevator are required by the
  California Building Code for accessibility compliance.

  It is the opinion of staff that the request meets the findings for granting of a variance. The
  variance request is limited in scope and will allow the operator to bring access to the rooftop

  9
   in compliance with accessibility requirements. The roof deck improvements otherwise
  have a maximum height of 22 feet 10 inches to the top of the parapet wall, well under the
  required height, well below the 28-foot height limit. This is a regulatory constraint that is
  applicable to all properties within the Commercial zone, and to all properties generally
  throughout the city, and that in this instance limit properties for developing to the full extent
  permitted in the municipal code. The height required to accommodate the staircase
  enclosure and LULA elevator is within the average height required for such installations.
  Purchase of specialized equipment could potentially reduce the height of the elevator
  tower, but a height variance would still be required for both the elevator tower and staircase
  enclosure due to construction limitations.

  Therefore, the proposed variances may be granted in conformance with the findings of the
  municipal code, as the strict application of the Zoning Ordinance would deprive the subject
  property of privileges enjoyed by other property in the vicinity and under identical zoning
  classification.

2. Any variance granted shall be subject to such conditions as will assure that the
  adjustment thereby authorized shall not constitute a grant of special privileges
  inconsistent with the limitations upon other properties in the vicinity and zone in
  which such property is situated.

  The applicant is requesting a variance to allow up to 32 feet in height to accommodate the
  enclosure for the staircase enclosures and Limited Use Limited Access (LULA) elevator
  shaft. The stairs and elevators will facilitate access to the roof deck and rooftop mechanical
  area. Both staircases and the elevator are required by the California Building Code for
  accessibility compliance.

  The variance request is limited in scope and will allow the operator to bring access to the
  rooftop in compliance with accessibility requirements. The roof deck improvements have
  a maximum height of 22 feet 10 inches to the top of the parapet wall, well under the
  required height, well below the 28-foot height limit, and otherwise comply with all
  development standards, and within the scope of permitted uses, for the Commercial zone.

  Therefore, granting of the requested variances does not constitute granting of special
  privileges as the variance allows development of the property within the parameters
  intended for the Commercial zone.

3. A variance shall not be granted for a parcel of property which authorizes a use or
  activity which is not otherwise expressly authorized by the zone regulation governing
  the parcel of property.

  Restaurant and bar uses are conditionally permitted uses within the C zone. The application
  does not include a request for any use that is not permitted within the zoning district.

4. No variances shall be granted which reduce or adversely affect access to or along the
  shoreline, including physical or visual qualities of access.

  10
   The project site is located approximately 150 feet from the mean high tide line of Avalon Bay.
  The site is not adjacent to, nor provides direct or indirect visual or physical access to, the
  shoreline of Avalon Bay, coastal hillsides or bluffs, or other significant viewsheds identified
  in the Avalon Local Coastal Plan.

  5. The variance shall be consistent with the Local Coastal Program.

  The proposed project implements Avalon General Plan/Local Coastal Plan and Local
  Coastal Program goals and policies as outlined in Conditional Use Permit Finding #1 and
  Coastal Development Permit Findings #1 and 2.

Site Plan Review:

The proposed project requires approval of a Site Plan per AMC Section 9-8.201. AMC Section 9-
8.203 sets forth the required findings for approval of a Site Plan Review as follows:

  1. Every use, development of land and application of development standards shall take
  place in compliance with all applicable provisions of this title. (AMC Section 9-
  8.203.a)

  With the requested variance for building height, the proposed project complies with all
  development standards as set forth in AMC for development on the project site in the
  Commercial (C) zone as discussed in Conditional Use Permit Findings #1 through 5 and
  Variance Findings #1 thought 5.

  whether the proposed project conforms with the Avalon General Plan, the Local Coastal
  Plan for Avalon, as well as the Avalon Zoning and Affordable Housing Ordinances, as
  applicable.

  •  General Plan/Local Coastal Plan: The Commercial (C) zoning designation of the
  project site is consistent with the General Plan land use designation of Commercial (C).

  As previously discussed in Conditional Use Permit Finding #1, the proposed project
  implements the following General Plan Goals and Policies: Policy II-9 of the Land Use
  Element.

  •  California Coastal Act: The proposed project complies with the following sections of
  the Coastal Act:

  8
   Section 30250:

  “(a) New residential, commercial, or industrial development, except as otherwise
  provided in this division, shall be located within, contiguous with, or in close proximity
  to, existing developed areas able to accommodate it or, where such areas are not able
  to accommodate it, in other areas with adequate public services and where it will not
  have significant adverse effects, either individually or cumulatively, on coastal
  resources. In addition, land divisions, other than leases for agricultural uses, outside
  existing developed areas shall be permitted only where 50 percent of the usable parcels
  in the area have been developed and the created parcels would be no smaller than the
  average size of surrounding parcels.”

  The project site is located within the urban center of Avalon, on an existing developed
  parcel surrounded by other commercial and residential uses. The project site is directly
  abutting the Clarrisa Avenue public right-of-way and is adequately served by all
  necessary utilities in order for the proposed use to operate at the property. The project
  site is not located on the coastline or adjacent coastal bluff or hillside and does not
  impede any designated coastal viewshed as identified in the Avalon Local Coastal Plan.
  Therefore, the project site can accommodate the proposed project and will not have an
  individual or cumulative effect on coastal resources.

  Section 30251:

  “The scenic and visual qualities of coastal areas shall be considered and protected as
  a resource of public importance. Permitted development shall be sited and designed to
  protect views to and along the ocean and scenic coastal areas, to minimize the
  alteration of natural land forms, to be visually compatible with the character of
  surrounding areas, and, where feasible, to restore and enhance visual quality in
  visually degraded areas. New development in highly scenic areas such as those
  designated in the California Coastline Preservation and Recreation Plan prepared by
  the Department of Parks and Recreation and by local government shall be subordinate
  to the character of its setting.”

  The project site is located within the city center of Avalon, on an urbanized parcel that
  is located in the “Flats” on the west side Clarissa Avenue between Crescent Avenue
  and Third Street. The proposed project is visually compatible with the mass and scale
  of surrounding commercial and mixed use development, and fits into the character of
  the Avalon skyline. The project will enhance the visual quality of the area through
  remodeling of an existing building in the Spanish/Mexican colonial architectural style,
  consistent with other developments within the city. The project site is not located in a
  scenic area identified in the Avalon Local Coastal Plan or in the California Coastline
  Preservation and Recreation Plan.

•  Commercial Zone Development Standards: The proposed project, with the approval of
  requested variance for height, complies with the development standards as set forth in

   AMC Section 9-6.204 for buildings in the Commercial (C) zone and the Avalon
  Municipal Code.

  •  Affordable Housing Ordinance: AMC Section 9-11.104.d requires that any new
  commercial development shall provide rental housing for at least 50% of the peak
  season employees. “New Commercial Development” is defined in AMC Section 9-
  11.103 as:

  “Any real property that both seeks to commence or expand commercial operations
  within the City of Avalon for which employees will be hired or transferred and: 1) a
  new structure will be built requiring City planning entitlements; 2) an existing structure
  will increase its footprint by 50% or more for purposes of continued or expanded
  commercial purposes; or 3) a residential structure or structures will be converted for
  commercial purposes.”

  The proposed project is an existing commercial business that will not increase the

PROJECT DESCRIPTION – ARCHITECTURAL DESIGN

This project entails the proposed exterior façade and interior remodel to the existing 4,498 square foot
Mi Casita Restaurant with Bar and a new 1,157 square foot roof terrace addition.

The existing building is located mid-block on the north side of Clarissa Avenue in Avalon’s central
commercial district one block from the harbor. Although the building has undergone several remodels
since its initial construction in 1972, it is not designated as a historic structure by any agency or group.
The redesign seeks to modernize the property while respecting its roots as a Mexican residential-style
restaurant with a bar.

Key exterior upgrades will focus on refreshed finishes, updated lighting, and improved pedestrian
appeal. The addition of architectural lighting will enhance the restaurant’s welcoming atmosphere
during evening hours, complementing the vibrant energy of the surrounding neighborhood. Existing
restaurant signage will remain in place, maintaining continuity in the building’s visual identity, and are
shown on elevations and listed on the sign schedule.

Interior improvements will include remodeled dining areas, restrooms, and kitchen facilities, ensuring a
cohesive and functional space for both staff and patrons. The addition of the third-floor rooftop dining
terrace will provide patrons with a new outdoor dining experience, offering views of the harbor and
enhancing the overall appeal of the restaurant.

With these new enhancements, the scale and massing of the building will remain consistent with
thoughtful design choices that respect the pedestrian character of Clarissa Avenue and the surrounding
properties. This remodel positions Mi Casita Restaurant as a revitalized, yet familiar cornerstone of
Avalon’s central commercial district.

ROOF TERRACE. New Roof Terrace addition, accessible by elevator and two interior stairs, provides
a unique third level dining and bar experience. New glass windscreens and radiant heaters provide
for guest comfort. Set back from the neighboring residential uses to the north [Pavilion Hotel] and west
[213 Clarissa] the Terrace provides guest views toward the harbor and distant ocean views along with
views to the ‘Terraces’ to the south.

The new Roof Terrace level respects the massing of the original building flat roof form. Roof Terrace
level includes new enclosed stairs, the elevator lobby, plus exterior dining and exterior bar. The roof
area connected by service stair to the second level ‘back of house’ shall remain as it provides the
required access to the roof top mechanical area.

 ACCESSIBILTY. In order for all three levels to be fully accessible, per current California Accessibility
codes, the installation of a Limited Use Limited Access [LULA] elevator and two exit stairs is required.
This elevator requires a 6ft by 6ft overhead mechanical shaft which extends above the 28 foot
maximum code height by approximately 4 feet. The required exit stair enclosures also exceed the 28
foot maximum height by 1’- 6” for a portion of the roof. In these two cases we are asking the Planning
Commission to allow these exceptions to allow Accessible upgrade features.

All new and existing roof top mechanical units shall be screened from public street views. Additional
noise-reduction screen features are included.

OCCUPANCY. Proposed total maximum building occupancy by 2022 California Building Code is 321
persons pending Building Department and Fire Department review of the existing building and
proposed renovation plans per CBC as adopted by the City of Avalon.

RESTAURANT OPERATIONS. Mi Casita Restaurant and Bar is a year-round establishment which
serves affordable, family-friendly Mexican food and bar menu to residents and visitors in the town of
Avalon on Catalina Island. The restaurant, which is family-owned and operated, has been in operation
for over a decade at this location. The restaurant employs cooks, servers, kitchen staff, and managers
who all live on the island either full or part-time.

Once completed, the proposed remodel and expansion of the Restaurant and Bar with new Roof
Terrace exterior patio will have approximately 170 seats total. The First Floor will seat approximately
67 guests; the Second Floor will seat approximately 57 guests; and the Roof Terrace will seat
approximately 46 guests.

The existing restaurant currently has a total of 189 seats.

PROPOSED HOURS OF OPERATION. As with many businesses in Avalon, actual operating hours are
seasonal, based on fluctuations in weather, commercial ferry schedules, and cruise ship traffic.

Proposed Restaurant and Bar hours are from 7am to 11 pm Sunday thru Thursday. Friday and
Saturday hours are from 7am to 12pm.

Proposed Roof Terrace hours are from 9am to 9pm Sunday thru Thursday and Friday and Saturday
from 9am to 10pm. Roof Terrace will also be available for private events on a limited basis during the
same operating hours.

Alcohol service is proposed for all three levels, provided under a new Conditional Use Permit, for the
same hours described above.

AMPLIFIED MUSIC. No outdoor entertainment is being proposed for the Roof Terrace level at this
time. All amplified music, including any live entertainment, shall be restricted to the interior space of
the ground and second floors. A separate permit for amplified “background” music on the roof will
be petitioned to the city in separate permit once the operation has been open for a summer season.

 EMPLOYEES. Typical total number of employees [servers, managers, and kitchen staff] on site at one
time is anticipated to be 14 at peak summer shifts. Shifts will vary with time of day, day of the week,
and seasonally. All staff enter and leave thru the main entry door on Clarissa. There are no back
entrances to the alley behind.

EMPLOYEE HOUSING REQUIREMENTS. As a long-time island family and employer, we have always
supported and actively participated in providing affordable housing for permanent and seasonal
employees on Catalina. It is reasonable for employers who make changes to their operations that
increase the demand for permanent and seasonal workers to actively participate in housing those
workers.

However, after reviewing the applicable codes, we do not believe that our proposed remodel exceeds
the statutory threshold that would make this a condition of approval (see calculation on Site Plan
A1.00.0).

Currently, we employ full-time, part-time, and seasonal staff, and we assist in securing housing for them
on a case-by-case basis. We own multiple residential units in Avalon, some of which accommodate our
seasonal staff as needed. Additionally, many of our workers are long-time island residents.

We do not anticipate needing to hire a significant number of new employees as a result of the
remodel. Based on our experience, during the busiest weeks of the year, many of our employees
voluntarily work overtime to supplement their income, which helps offset reduced hours during the off-
season.

As a family-operated business, we have several positions such as host, general manager, runner, and
office manager that are filled by our own family members on a full- or part-time basis.

For these reasons, we do not foresee the remodel having a substantial impact on our staffing needs or
the demand for additional employee housing.

REASONS FOR APPROVAL. The proposed renovation and expansion of the restaurant, including the
addition of a new rooftop terrace, will enhance the character and appeal of Clarissa Avenue and its
surrounding neighborhood. This thoughtful project aligns with Avalon’s commitment to maintaining a
vibrant and welcoming Downtown Commercial District. By improving the restaurant’s facilities, the
project will support its continued financial success, contributing to Avalon’s post-COVID economic
recovery.

The family owners, managers, and local staff have established a reputation as dedicated and
considerate members of the community for many years. This project represents an investment in both
the restaurant’s future and the broader vitality of Avalon.

We respectfully request your support and approval to make their vision a reality.

emergency exit out the rear of the building. In addition, the Project proposes three windows on the
left side of the building in the proposed space. Proposed plans are included as Attachment 3 to this
report.

  DISCUSSION AND ANALYSIS

Issue 1 – Variance for third story and maximum floor area for construction of a 360 square
foot bonus room, partially below grade:

Per AMC Section 9-5.305.e.1.i, on lots with an average slope of 14° or less, no portion of the
building may exceed a height greater than 28 feet above the lot's natural surface and shall not be
more than two levels. Lots with a steeper grade may increase up to three levels. There is no
definition for “level” in the municipal code, but levels may consist of finished spaces such as
stories, basements, or open decks depending on the configuration of the building or structure.

The existing building the unit is located in meets the overall height requirement and is currently
two stories. The existing crawlspace does not meet the municipal code definitions for a story or
basement (AMC Sections 9-3.602 and 9-3.619) as it is not a space with a floor or ceiling.
According to the project plans, the average slope of grade under the unit is 9° (degrees).
Construction of a new lower-level bonus family room and bathroom would result in the unit
becoming three stories in height, which is not permitted based on the average slope of the lot.
Therefore, granting of a Variance is required to allow construction of the new living space as
proposed by the applicant.

It is the opinion of staff that a Variance may be granted for the new third story buildout based on
the following considerations:

  •  The proposed project meets all other development standards for a three-level building in
  the MD zone, including height and floor area. Therefore, it will comply with existing height
  and massing standards and will remain visually compatible with the surrounding Sol Vista
  Condominium community.

  4
   •  Allowing the applicant to expand their living space within the existing footprint of their
  unit will have minimal impact on the privacy of surrounding properties. It will not decrease
  existing setbacks, and the space will be partially below grade, with no windows or decks
  that can look into the private spaces of surrounding residences.

  •  Other units within the greater Sol Vista Condominium community have previously been
  granted approval for lower level, third story buildouts by the City, including 86 and 87 Sol
  Vista within the same community. Therefore, approval of the variance would not grant the
  applicant any special privileges inconsistent with existing property development patterns.

Findings and conditions are provided in the staff report and draft resolution to support the granting
of a Variance. In particular, Condition #6 states that no conversion of the new bonus room space
to create a new bedroom shall be permitted without appropriate review by the Avalon Planning
and Building Department and provision of a will serve letter from Southern California Edison
Company (“SCE”) that adequate freshwater allocation is available for the proposed conversion.

California Environmental Quality Act:

The proposed project is categorically exempt from the provisions of the California Environmental
Quality Act (CEQA) per State CEQA Guidelines 15301 (Class 1 – Existing Facilities) because it
has no potential to have a significant effect on the environment.

The Class 1 exemption includes the operation, repair, maintenance, permitting, leasing, licensing,
or minor alteration of existing public or private structures, facilities, mechanical equipment, or
topographical features, involving negligible or no expansion of use. The project involves an
addition to an existing residential townhome within an established residential community totaling
less than 50 percent of the floor area of the unit. As such, the project is not expected to have
significant environmental impact on the surrounding area.

Further, none of the exceptions to the use of categorical exemptions stated in State CEQA
Guidelines section 15300.2 apply: The Project is not located in a sensitive environment because it
is proposed in an area already developed for residential uses. No cumulative impact would occur
from this Project’s approval because only a single application has been submitted, and no future
development is proposed. There will be no significant effect on the environment because the
Project is only for an addition of space to an existing residence that would have only minor impacts.
No damage to scenic resources will occur because this Project will occur on an existing developed
residential site, and other than the requested variance for an additional level, is consistent with
adopted development standards. The project is not located on a hazardous waste site, and the

  DISCUSSION AND ANALYSIS

Issue 1 – Variance for third story and maximum floor area to construct a 395 square foot
third story family room and bathroom addition partially below grade:

Per AMC Section 9-5.305.e.1.i, on lots with an average slope of 14° or less, no portion of the
building may exceed a height greater than 28 feet above the lot's natural surface and shall not be
more than two levels. Lots with a steeper grade may increase up to three levels. There is no
definition for “level” in the municipal code, but levels may consist of finished spaces such as
stories, basements, or open decks depending on the configuration of the building or structure.

The existing unit meets the overall height requirement and is currently two stories. The existing
crawlspace does not meet the municipal code definitions for a story or basement (AMC Sections
9-3.602 and 9-3.619) as it is not a space with a floor or ceiling. According to the project plans, the
current average slope of grade under the unit is 7°. Excavation of the existing crawlspace to
construct a new lower-level playroom, hobby room and bathroom would result in the unit
becoming three stories in height, which is not permitted based on the average slope of the lot.
Therefore, granting a Variance is required to allow construction of the new living space to create
a third floor.

Per AMC Section 9-5.305.e.3.i, on lots with an average slope of 14° or less, the total gross floor
area shall not exceed 150% of the gross lot area for properties with three stories. The AMC defines
the floor area as:

  “the sum of the gross areas of all interior space unless specifically excluded from this
  definition of the several floors of a building, measured from the interior wall surfaces,

  4
   including (1) stairwells; (2) carports, porches, and balconies where there is a full roof over
  the feature and greater than 45% enclosure on three sides, including glass enclosures; (3)
  basements and attics where the ceiling height is seven feet or greater or otherwise qualify
  as a story; and (4) enclosed garages, but excluding from the calculation that area within an
  enclosed garage equal to the dimensions of an autoette or full-sized vehicle parking space,
  as appropriate under the planning approvals” (AMC Section 9-3.606 “F” Definitions).”

The existing building the unit is located in is currently legal, non-conforming, as the current floor
area is 110% (1,057 sq. ft.) of the gross lot area, which exceeds the two-story requirement of 100%
floor area of the gross lot area. The existing crawlspace does not meet the municipal code
definitions for a story or basement (AMC Sections 9-3.602 and 9-3.619) and does not account to
the existing floor area ratio. According to the project plans, the average slope of grade under the
unit is 7°. Construction of a new lower-level playroom, hobby room and bathroom would result in
the unit becoming three stories in height, increasing the floor area ratio to 152% (1,452 sq. ft.)
which is not permitted based on the average slope of the lot (AMC Section 9-5.305.e.3.i).
Therefore, granting a Variance is required to allow construction of the new living space increasing
the floor area as proposed by the applicant.

It is the opinion of staff that a Variance may be granted for the new third story buildout based on
the following considerations:

  •  The proposed project meets all other development standards for a three-level building in
  the MD-R zone, including height and parking. The proposed addition will take place
  entirely within the existing building footprint. Therefore, it will comply with existing
  height and massing standards and will remain visually compatible with the surrounding Sol
  Vista Condominium community.

  •  Allowing the applicant to expand their living space within the existing footprint of their
  unit will have minimal impact on the privacy of surrounding properties. It will not decrease
  existing setbacks, and the space will be partially below grade and entirely within the
  existing building footprint. There will be no windows or decks that can look into the private
  spaces of surrounding residences.

  •  Other units within the greater Sol Vista Condominium community have previously been
  granted approval for lower level, third story buildouts by the City, including 86 and 87 Sol
  Vista within the same community. Therefore, approval of the variance would not grant the
  applicant any special privileges inconsistent with existing property development patterns.

Findings and conditions are provided in the staff report and draft resolution to support the granting
of a Variance. In particular, Condition #6 states that no conversion of the playroom and/or hobby
room space to create a new bedroom shall be permitted without appropriate review by the Planning
& Building Department and provision of a will serve letter from Southern California Edison
Company (“SCE”) that adequate freshwater allocation is available for the proposed conversion.

  PROJECT DESCRIPTION

The applicant proposes to develop two new units and an office at the rear of the property within a
1,343 square foot two-story residential. The first floor of the building will consist of a one-bedroom
Accessory Dwelling Unit (ADU) with a full bathroom, kitchen and living room, a total square
footage of 525 square feet. Entry to the first story ADU will be from the south side of the new
structure. The second floor is a one-bedroom unit with a full bathroom, kitchen and living room,
totaling 657 square feet. Entry to the second story unit will be from the rear of the property with a
new staircase up to the upper unit. The accessory office will be associated with the main residence
and attached to the proposed building but will not be interconnected with either of the new dwelling
units new. The office is 161 square feet. The proposed project also includes a new retaining wall
that will either replace the existing retaining wall or be built to support the existing retaining wall.

create privacy between all units. In addition, the existing staircase in the rear of the property will
be replaced to provide entry to the main single family residence outdoor space from the rear of the
property. The applicant prefers to seek approval for the entire proposed structure at once, rather
than submitting an application for only an ADU. If the Planning Commission approves the
application, the ADU will be reviewed separately and ministerially by the Planning Department,
in accordance with AMC Chapter 9-5, Article 6 “Accessory Dwelling Units.”

  considered on the basis of suitable and functional development design, but is not
  intended that such approval be interpreted to require a particular style or type of
  architecture. (AMC Section 9-8.203.c)

  3
   The project site is located at the intersection of Upper Olive Street and Vieudelou Avenue.
  This area, generally known as “the hills”, is predominantly developed with single-family
  residences of various heights depending on the slope of the lot. The design elements in the
  proposed plans are consistent with the established scale of the buildings and structures
  within the community and will not stand out as inconsistent with existing development on
  the site or in the vicinity.

Variance:

Variance approval is required for side and rear setback reductions per AMC Section 9-5.305.d.
AMC Chapter 9-8.405 sets forth the required findings for approval of a Variance as follows:

  1. Variances from the terms of the Zoning Ordinance shall be granted only when,
  because of special circumstances applicable to the property including size, shape,
  topography, location or surroundings, the strict application of the Zoning Ordinance
  deprives such property of privileges enjoyed by other property in the vicinity and
  under identical zoning classification.

  The urban fabric of Avalon is relatively compact, with approximately 80-90 acres of
  existing development already located within the valley floor and the immediately
  surrounding hillsides. Individually owned lots in Avalon comprise less than 1% of the total
  city acreage. As such, there is minimal available land for construction of new residential
  units to supply diverse housing options for long-term residents. Therefore, it is important
  to maximize the use of residentially zoned land within the city within the development
  parameters of each zoning district, so long as it is consistent with overall community
  character.

  Additional residential units on single-family lots is permitted within the MD zone, where
  the size and story of those units is dependent upon the slope of the lot. The proposed
  building footprint will be constructed between the rear property line and the existing
  retaining wall, which limits the area to build. In addition, the second-floor unit will be
  divided from the main residence with a fence that bounds the existing main resident
  outdoor space. The existing retaining wall creates an obstacle to creating adequately sized
  dwelling units.

  Construction of adequately sized units, while also providing trash space, outdoor space and
  the required parking, will require setback reductions from the required setbacks of 10 feet
  on all sides. However, the proposed project meets all other development standards for
  additional units in the MD zone, including height, floor area, lot coverage, and parking.
  Therefore, it will comply with existing height and massing standards and will remain
  visually compatible with the surrounding community.

  4
 2. Any variance granted shall be subject to such conditions as will assure that the
  adjustment thereby authorized shall not constitute a grant of special privileges
  inconsistent with the limitations upon other properties in the vicinity and zone in
  which such property is situated.

  The project is proposed on a lot located in “the hills”, with an irregular shape, location and
  topography. The lot currently contains an existing retaining wall located 34 feet from the
  rear property line, which limits the construction of additional residential units. In addition,
  the setback requirements also limit this construction, where variance approval will create
  feasible and efficient use of the space and allow the development to construct the allowable
  density in the zone. Therefore, approval of the variance would not grant the applicant any
  special privileges inconsistent with existing property development patterns. Condition #6
  of the draft Planning Commission resolution states that no conversion of the office room
  space to create a new bedroom shall be permitted without appropriate review by the
  Planning & Building Department and provision of a will serve letter from Southern
  California Edison Company (“SCE”) that adequate freshwater allocation is available for
  the proposed conversion

3. A variance shall not be granted for a parcel of property which authorizes a use or
  activity which is not otherwise expressly authorized by the zone regulation governing
  the parcel of property.

  The detached residential buildings are permitted within the Multiple Residential, Medium
  Density (MD) zone. The MD zone allows a density up to 20 units per acre, which allows
  the project site to have two residential units. The project site currently has one main single-
  family residential unit, and is proposing one additional unit and one ADU, for a total of
  three units. However, per AMC Section 9-7.602.b, ADUs do not count towards the
  calculation of density, therefore the density of development conforms to the underlying
  development standard. The proposed project will not change the use of the property or the
  overall character of the community.

4. No variances shall be granted which reduce or adversely affect access to or along the
  shoreline, including physical or visual qualities of access.

  The project site is located over 800 feet from the mean high tide line of Avalon Bay. The
  site is not adjacent to, nor provides direct or indirect visual or physical access to, the
  shoreline of Avalon Bay, coastal hillsides or bluffs, or other significant viewsheds
  identified in the Avalon Local Coastal Plan.

5.  The variance shall be consistent with the Local Coastal Program.

  The proposed project implements Avalon General Plan/Local Coastal Plan and Local
  Coastal Program goals and policies as outlined in Coastal Development Permit Findings
  #1 and 2.

  5
 Coastal Development Permit:
The City of Avalon is located entirely within the Coastal Zone. A Coastal Development Permit is
required per AMC Section 9-8.102. The project is not located within the 300-foot appealable
boundary of the Coastal Zone and qualifies as development that requires the local issuance a
Coastal Development Permit in accordance with AMC Section 9-8, dependent on the following
findings:

  1. The use is in conformance with the certified Local Coastal Program. (AMC 9-
  8.103.d.1)

  Determination of conformance for projects within the City of Avalon includes analysis of
  whether the proposed project conforms with the Avalon General Plan, the Local Coastal
  Plan for Avalon, as well as the Avalon Zoning and Affordable Housing Ordinances, as
  applicable.

  •  General Plan/Local Coastal Plan: The Multiple Residential, Medium Density (MD)
  zoning designation of the project site is consistent with the General Plan land use
  designation of Medium Density Residential (MDR).

  The proposed project implements the following General Plan Goals and Policies:

  Policy II-1 of the Land Use Element:

  “Use the City’s Zoning Ordinance and any applicable residential, commercial, resort,
  and open space design standards to guide the character of development and ensure
  compatibility with existing residential, commercial, resort, and open space uses.”

  The proposed project involves construction of a two-unit residential building on a
  developed residential property. The proposed project requests a variance for a setback
  reduction in the rear and side yard setbacks and meets all other development standards
  for a residential development in the MD zone, including height, floor area, parking and
  lot coverage. This area, generally known as “the hills”, is predominantly developed
  with single-family residences of various heights depending on the slope of the lot,
  including two- and three-story buildings. Therefore, it will comply with existing height
  and massing standards and will remain visually compatible with the surrounding
  neighborhood.

  •  California Coastal Act: The proposed project complies with the following sections of
  the Coastal Act:

  Section 30250:

  “(a) New residential, commercial, or industrial development, except as otherwise
  provided in this division, shall be located within, contiguous with, or in close proximity
  to, existing developed areas able to accommodate it or, where such areas are not able
  to accommodate it, in other areas with adequate public services and where it will not

  6
   have significant adverse effects, either individually or cumulatively, on coastal
  resources. In addition, land divisions, other than leases for agricultural uses, outside
  existing developed areas shall be permitted only where 50 percent of the usable parcels
  in the area have been developed and the created parcels would be no smaller than the
  average size of surrounding parcels.”

  The proposed project involves the development of an two-unit residential building on
  a developed residential lot in an urbanized area of the city. The Project meets the
  general requirements for overall lot coverage and floor area, and there will be no change
  of use of the project site. The project site is located over 600 feet from the nearest
  coastline (Avalon Bay) and does not contain any coastal resources, publicly accessible
  coastal viewpoints, or coastal access points. Therefore, the area can accommodate the
  proposed project and will not have an individual or cumulative effect on coastal
  resources.

  •  Multiple Residential, Medium Density Development Standards: The applicant is
  requesting a reduction of the rear yard setback from the required 10 feet to 6’6” in the
  rear of the property. The existing two-story single-family residence has an existing side
  yard setback of approximately 3’2”. The applicant is also requesting a 1-foot reduction
  in the rear setback on the second floor only, in order to increase the upper unit to a 2-
  bedroom unit versus a 1-bedroom unit with a future water allocation and application.
  This request to reduce setbacks will still allow feasible construction on the site as well
  as providing adequately sized housing. The proposed project meets all other
  development standards for a residential development in the MD zone, including height,
  floor area, parking and lot coverage.

  •  Affordable Housing Ordinance: This ordinance is not applicable to the proposed project
  since the proposal does not include the development of five or more residential units.

  2. For all development seaward of the nearest public highway to the shoreline, the
  proposed development conforms to the public access and recreation policies of
  Chapter 3 of the Coastal Act. (AMC 9-8.103.d.2)

  The project site is not seaward of Crescent Avenue, which is the nearest public access to
  the shoreline. The proposed project involves development of a two-unit residential building
  and on-site improvements to an existing developed property in a residential area of the city.
  The project does not involve a change in land use, density, or intensity that will result in
  increased demand for public access and recreation opportunities. Furthermore, the project
  does not include any building or site modification that could block or impede existing public
